name: Opus Value
strategy: A trend book that owns only what the tape currently confirms: energy (at 3-month highs) sized up, healthcare and quality as the leading defensive trends, a small consumer-discretionary short, and 42% cash while gold, momentum and the Treasury short have broken trend.
reassessment_note: Daily closes show three of last week's six legs now fighting the tape. On 10-22/23 GLD fell to a fresh 3-month low (366.61, below its 20d 379 and 50d 395), GDX broke down to 80.20 (-13% over the month, below its 20d 86.6 and 50d 92.9), and the leg is -7.3%. A trend book should not wait for the -15% stop on a trend that has already broken, so I am cutting it. MTUM is -8.8% over the month and below both moving averages; semis/momentum leadership has not come back, so I am cutting the starter. TLT has rallied from 77.1 to 81.3 and is back above its 50-day as 10-year yields eased from a 24-year high. The short is losing (-2.4%), and the Fed decision on 10-28 is a binary rates event I do not want to be short duration into, so I am covering it. Energy is the cleanest trend (XLE +10.8% over the month, at a 3-month high), so I am sizing it up from 16% to 22%. XLV (+5.5% over the month, above both averages, near its high, after UNH's beat-and-raise) is the new leader and replaces the gold sleeve. QUAL (flat, around its averages) and the XLY short stay as they are. Round 3 novelty: the Round 2 book holds single names (UNH, CI, XOM, CVX, ADBE), GLD and ETH, and none of those symbols is in this book, so same-direction symbol overlap is 0%. Healthcare and energy are thematically adjacent to Round 2, but I hold them here via sector ETFs on a trend rule, not a value one.

positions.thesis: Strongest trend on my screen: XLE closed at a 3-month high of 69.33 on 10-23, +10.8% over the month and well above its 20d (65.4) and 50d (64.3), with oil supported by the unresolved Strait of Hormuz standoff. I am sizing it up from 16% to 22% because it is the only sleeve where both price trend and macro driver agree. The 10% stop sits below the late-September breakout zone.

New leader. XLV is at 179.28, +5.5% over the month, above its 20d (172.5) and 50d (171.1) and within about 1% of its 3-month high, helped by UNH's 10-13 beat-and-raise (MCR 88.4%) re-rating managed care. It also offers defensive leadership while SPY sits below its moving averages. It takes the risk budget freed by cutting GDX, and the 8% stop puts the exit back below the 50-day.

Kept at 14% as the broad-market anchor. QUAL is flat on the month and essentially at its 50-day (222.8 vs 223.4), so the trend is neutral rather than broken, and quality balance sheets suit a regime of near-5% yields. The leg is only -1.1%. The 10% stop is held as originally set.

Kept as a small hedge. XLY at 113.10 sits below its 50-day (113.4) and 7% under its 3-month high, and $95+ oil with near-5% long yields squeezes discretionary spending. The leg is +1.2%. It stays small because the trend signal is weak and short squeezes into a Fed decision are possible, so it has a tight 8% stop.
